Fri, September 25, 2026 at 3:38 PM EDT 1 min read
CL=F
^DJI
^GSPC
^IXIC

(Updates with index/price moves and geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes advanced as crude oil prices declined after Iran floated a conditional proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks over its nuclear program.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to 27,062.3, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.9% to 51,795.2, and the S&P 500 advanced 0.4% to 7,738.8 ahead of Friday's close.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key crude and energy chokepoint, and restart talks on its nuclear program if Washington accepts its conditions, CNBC reported Friday, citing Araghchi's remarks on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

"The conditions we have asked the US to meet are nothing new, nothing more than what was already in the Islamabad [memorandum of understanding]," Araghchi reportedly said.

The front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract dropped 2.1% to $92.62 per barrel, and the global benchmark North Sea Brent retreated 1.7% to $104.78 per barrel.

US Treasury yields traded mixed, with the 10-year steady at 5.17% while the two-year dropped 3.5 basis points to 4.86%.

Gold futures edged up 0.4% to $4,316.1, and silver futures advanced 1% to $64.64.

CECO Environmental trades at $73.39 and has moved in lockstep with the market. Its shares have returned 18.2% over the last six months while the S&P 500 has gained 16.9%.

Is now the time to buy CECO Environmental, or should you be careful about including it in your portfolio? Get the full breakdown from our expert analysts, it's free.

Why Is CECO Environmental Not Exciting?

We're passing on CECO Environmental for now. Here are three reasons why CECO doesn't excite us, plus one stock we'd rather own.

1. Fewer Distribution Channels Limit Its Ceiling

With $903.2 million in revenue over the past 12 months, CECO Environmental is a small player in the business services space, which sometimes brings disadvantages compared to larger competitors benefiting from economies of scale and numerous distribution channels. On the bright side, it can grow faster because it has more room to expand.

2. Shrinking Adjusted Operating Margin

Adjusted operating margin is one of the best measures of profitability because it tells us how much money a company takes home after subtracting all core expenses, like marketing and R&D. It also removes various one-time costs to paint a better picture of normalized profits.

Analyzing the trend in its profitability, CECO Environmental's adjusted operating margin decreased by 4.8 percentage points over the last five years. This raises questions about the company's expense base because its revenue growth should have given it leverage on its fixed costs, resulting in better economies of scale and profitability. CECO Environmental's performance was poor no matter how you look at it - it shows that costs were rising and it couldn't pass them onto its customers. Its adjusted operating margin for the trailing 12 months was breakeven.

CECO Environmental Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin (Non-GAAP)
3. High Debt Levels Increase Risk

As long-term investors, the risk we care about most is the permanent loss of capital, which can happen when a company goes bankrupt or raises money from a disadvantaged position. This is separate from short-term stock price volatility, something we are much less bothered by.

CECO Environmental's $727.7 million of debt exceeds the $63.85 million of cash on its balance sheet. Furthermore, its 6× net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio (based on its EBITDA of $113.6 million over the last 12 months) shows the company is overleveraged.

CECO Environmental Net Debt Position

At this level of debt, incremental borrowing becomes increasingly expensive and credit agencies could downgrade the company's rating if profitability falls. CECO Environmental could also be backed into a corner if the market turns unexpectedly – a situation we seek to avoid as investors in high-quality companies.

Final Judgment

We cheer for all companies serving everyday consumers, but in the case of Royal Caribbean, we'll be cheering from the sidelines. Following the recent decline, the stock trades at 12.2× forward P/E (or $239.25 per share). This valuation is reasonable, but the company's shaky fundamentals present too much downside risk. 3. Previous Growth Initiatives Haven't Impressed

Growth gives us insight into a company's long-term potential, but how capital-efficient was that growth? A company's ROIC explains this by showing how much operating profit it makes compared to the money it has raised (debt and equity).

Royal Caribbean historically did a mediocre job investing in profitable growth initiatives. Its five-year average ROIC was 7.6%, somewhat low compared to the best consumer discretionary companies that consistently pump out 65%+.

Royal Caribbean Trailing 12-Month Free Cash Flow Margin
2. Mediocre Free Cash Flow Margin Limits Reinvestment Potential

If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.

Royal Caribbean has shown poor cash profitability relative to peers over the last two years, giving the company fewer opportunities to return capital to shareholders. Its free cash flow margin averaged 8.8%, below what we'd expect for a consumer discretionary business.

Royal Caribbean Passenger Cruise Days
1. Weak Growth in Passenger Cruise Days Points to Soft Demand

Revenue growth can be broken down into changes in price and volume (for companies like Royal Caribbean, our preferred volume metric is passenger cruise days). While both are important, the latter is the most critical to analyze because prices have a ceiling.

Royal Caribbean's passenger cruise days came in at 14.96 million in the latest quarter, and over the last two years, averaged 6.6% year-on-year growth. This performance was underwhelming and suggests it might have to lower prices or invest in product improvements to accelerate growth, factors that can hinder near-term profitability.

(Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data and company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes rose as crude oil prices fell after Iran floated a conditional proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks over its nuclear program, reigniting hopes of a deal to end the war that's choked energy markets.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to 27,084.8, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.8% to 51,753.1, and the S&P 500 advanced 0.5% to 7,740.6 after midday Friday. Energy and communication services led decliners, while technology and industrials topped gainers.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key crude and energy chokepoint, and restart talks on its nuclear program if Washington accepts its conditions, CNBC reported Friday, citing Araghchi's remarks on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

"The conditions we have asked the US to meet are nothing new, nothing more than what was already in the Islamabad [memorandum of understanding]," Araghchi reportedly said.

The front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract dropped 2.2% to $92.58 per barrel, and the global benchmark North Sea Brent retreated 1.9% to $104.57 per barrel.

US Treasury yields traded mixed, with the 10-year adding 3.8 basis points to 5.20% while the two-year was steady at 4.89%.

Gold futures edged up 0.4% to $4,316.1, and silver futures advanced 1% to $64.64.

In economic news, new orders for durable goods were flat in August from a 0.9% gain in July, versus expectations of a 0.3% decline in a Bloomberg-compiled survey. Excluding a 0.6% drop in transportation orders, new orders would have been up 0.3% in August after a 0.7% increase in July. Expectations were for a 0.6% gain.

The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index was revised higher to 48.1 for September from 47.8 in the preliminary estimate, versus expectations of a downward revision to 47.5 in a Bloomberg-compiled survey. The print is still below August's final 51.7 reading.

Respondents expected a 4.6% inflation rate over the next year and 3.4% annual inflation over the next five years, up from 4.0% and 3.3% respectively in August.

"Overall, interviews reveal broad agreement across the political spectrum that the outlook for the economy has weakened since the beginning of the year," Michigan said. "After particularly large declines in sentiment this month, Republican sentiment is now 20% lower than January 2026; Democrats are down 13% over the same period."

In company news, Meta Platforms' (META) Muse AI agent has strong early adoption, but uncertain monetization raises concerns, Oppenheimer said in a note. Muse saw about 340,000 US downloads per day, but even if downloads reached 500,000 per day for more than a year, 2027 revenue would rise only about 4%, the investment research outfit said. Meta's shares fell 3.4%, the Nasdaq's worst performer.
